title: Give every hband screen (reader pages, /admin pages, Blocked users and the forbidden page) one designed look in light and dark, from one shared stylesheet and layout
how_to_read: Each attempt is one line and a `details` filename in this same directory. Open a detail file ONLY when this index points you at one -- the summaries are here so you do not have to. `caused_by` is what sent the stage back; `changed` is what the attempt then touched, counted by kind. Several attempts in a row that were caused by the same stage and changed no `src` is a loop, not progress.

open.issue: One shared design system in one place: colour tokens for light AND dark, a type scale and a spacing scale: missing

Components covering links, buttons, text inputs/textareas, forms and form rows, notices, lists and tables, cards/panels, details/summary, badges and avatars, plus the admin needs: tables, destructive buttons and the two-step remove: missing
One shared base layout that every template takes; no page carries its own head, style block or inline styles: partial

Every reader screen (home and /reports/<slug> with report frame, like count, vote controls, comments and the feedback box with the sender's own messages and author replies; the show-all page; the branch page), signed in and signed out, shows the designed look: missing

Every /admin screen (admin.html, admin_report.html, admin_blocked.html) and the forbidden page shows the designed look, with the admin components (tables, destructive buttons, two-step remove): missing
Dark mode follows prefers-color-scheme with no manual light/dark switch: missing
No control or link is left in the browser default (checked by computed styles, not screenshots): missing
No horizontal scroll at a true 375 CSS px phone width on every screen: partial
Text and controls meet a stated contrast bar in both schemes (WCAG AA proposed): partial
report-frame-canvas-under-site-surface: V1 light: report A shows site #f3f1ea inside the frame (not white); dark stays white. V2 flips B.
Thread script: kept in the head behind a ThreadScript() method, giving byte-identical reader pages (practice, chosen), or the tag moved into main, giving a simpler data contract (crossdomain).
Header: inside page-start, so no page can forget it, with forbidden.html defining its own brand-only header (practice, chosen); or called by each page, with a shared "brand" partial (crossdomain).

Admin roles: class="primary" on Upload and class="danger" on Delete (practice), or frozen markup with form-action selectors (crossdomain, chosen). Neither button is pinned by a test, so this is a judgement of explicitness against one uniform 'bodies unchanged' rule.
Head: add `<meta name="color-scheme" content="light dark">` to avoid a white flash before the CSS loads (crossdomain), or keep the head verbatim for byte identity (practice, chosen).
Hidden states: a structural [hidden]:not(:target) guard (crossdomain, chosen), or a source check banning display on hidden-carrying hooks (practice).

internal/layout as a package (both, chosen), or practice's flagged trim: forbidden.html keeps its own head, pinned byte-equal to the server's "head", with no new package and no test edit, at the cost of the brief's 'no page carries its own head' bar.
Decoration: an avatar ring drawn with an opaque box-shadow and a CSS-border chevron on summaries. These are left to the frontend designer within the token contract.

The /admin pages and Blocked users are not in `screens`: the engine's seeded product signs in only as a non-owner, so it can reach the Not allowed page but not the admin pages, and `screens` holds at most 6. TestEveryScreenIsDesigned measures all three as the owner, in both schemes, at both widths, with details open.
Firefox and Safari were not run (O-017, owed to validate): only Chrome is driven here.

No confirmation step on 'Delete this report permanently', and /admin keeps its own owner line and Sign out beside the shared header's. The design filed both for a person because they change behaviour or content.
The engine's Fitness op=check was not run: the builder cannot. The three new rules are plain YAML scalars with no ': ' or ' #' in them, and the repo's lenient loader and corpus tests load them.

Q-012's decided enforcement (a fitness rule forbidding `<script` in report.html and layout.html) does not exist in fitness.yaml, and thread.js is loaded on the found home, report and branch pages. This slice moved the tag into internal/layout/templates/base.html and pinned it there in TestEveryPageTakesTheShell. A person should say whether Q-012 is amended to 'thread.js is the one allowed site script' or whether a fitness rule should also be written.

On the /admin table at 375 px, the word 'published' breaks mid-word ('publishe/d') because body cells use overflow-wrap: anywhere, which is what keeps the page from scrolling sideways. A fix could be a narrower Status column or a different wrap rule on that cell, if somebody wants it.

Cross-rule ordering of border shorthands (a later rule restating `border: 1px solid` after another rule set border-color to a token) is caught only inside one rule. A browser assertion that every bordered control's edge colour differs from its text colour would close it.

The engine's app command was Python-launcher based (#13 of the design); this build reports `go run ./internal/testutil/seeded -port {port}`. The engine's projects.app_command still has to be repointed by the engine for the photographs.
Architecture: internal/server (C-001) also imports internal/layout (C-008). Only the C-002 edge fits in this report's three architecture edits.

deviation: forbidden.html defines its "header" after page-end, not before page-start: TestEveryPageTakesTheShell requires a page to open with page-start, and the design's own contract said both. admin.html's uploadform already sits after page-end the same way.

deviation: .replies uses border-left: 1px solid; border-left-color: var(--thread) instead of leaving the shorthand with var(--thread) as M-add-1 said. phone_test reads the shorthand identically (a 1 px width; border-left-color is not read), so the 'no var() in an edge shorthand' rule has no exemption.

deviation: The forced hover pass applies the 3:1 boundary check only to controls that had a fill or edge at rest (tracked in a WeakSet). Quiet buttons (the header's Sign out) take a deliberately subtle --surface-2 hover tint, which is a change of state, not a boundary. Text contrast still applies to every forced control.
deviation: lintStylesheet also refuses clip-path (same class as the frame-reach properties), url(), transition and animation, which the design only listed as rules for later slices.

deviation: Added an optional page dump to TestEveryScreenIsDesigned, written only when HBAND_TEST_ARTIFACTS is set (an existing test setting), so a person can look at the screens. The test judges nothing from it.

deviation: Added fire/quiet corpus rows and a bounded_by entry for the three new fitness rules in internal/fitnessrules/testdata/rule_spellings.json. The fitnessrules tests did not require them, but a glob such as internal/layout/**/*.go is otherwise untested.

deviation: The design says a browser without light-dark() 'falls back to the browser-default look'. The built CSS follows the accepted finding M-add-1 instead: transparent fills, controls and panels keeping literal-width currentColor edges, and the focus ring surviving. This build contains no workaround for a defect outside the project, so there is no per-bug checkbox or notice to build.
